entry.title: Cat Coffin
entry.blurb: Although the cat is considered the most Egyptian of animals, as an object of worship the cat does not appear until late in Egyptian history.

source.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust

facts: The coffin is, of course, hollow, with an open bottom.
As usual, the animal’s tail is curled around its right side.
A necklace appears to have been incised or scratched into the finished bronze; faint traces are visible on the chest.

candidate.title: Cat Coffin
candidate.credit: The Cleveland Museum of Art. Gift of the John Huntington Art and Polytechnic Trust
candidate.description: Although the cat is considered the most Egyptian of animals, as an object of worship the cat does not appear until late in Egyptian history. This unusually large statue of a cat was made to hold the mummified remains of a sacred cat. The coffin is, of course, hollow, with an open bottom. As usual, the animal’s tail is curled around its right side. A necklace appears to have been incised or scratched into the finished bronze; faint traces are visible on the chest.
candidate.culture: Egypt, Greco-Roman period (332 BCE–395 CE), Ptolemaic dynasty (305–30 BCE)
